Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region. Publicado también por: Euronews. Fuente: Africanews.
item.dc:creator: editorial@africanews.com (Alexis Caraco)

item.title: Papa León XIV asegura que retomará gradualmente sus funciones tras operación en el pulmón
item.description: Miles de fieles se congregaron en la plaza de San Pedro para escuchar el rezo del Ángelus del papa León XIV, el día después de recibir el alta tras someterse a una operación en el pulmón derecho en la que le extirparon un tumor maligno. Además de la habitual oración de los domingos, León XIV dirigió unas palabras desde la ventana del Palacio Apostólico en las que aseguró que retomará sus actividades de forma gradual. Informe de nuestra corresponsal, Irene Savio. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: The next ayahuasca? Gabon fights to protect sacred plant from US drug companies
item.description: Iboga root, central to several Gabonese ritual traditions, is believed to have huge potential for use in treating addiction and some mental illnesses The temple is dark, its sandy floor edged with candles. People sit shoulder to shoulder beneath palm fronds hung from the rafters. Through the night, they swallow what they have come here for: a bitter root bark called iboga. Tabernanthe iboga is a slow-growing central African rainforest shrub, the root bark of which has long been used in several Gabonese ritual traditions. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Egypt pledges support for Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: Egypt announced its willingness to provide military assistance to Saudi Arabia to ensure its security and stability. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi convened the National Defence Council to discuss potential support amid Houthi assaults. These attacks have targeted key infrastructure, including Riyadh’s international airport and Saudi Aramco. Egypt has previously supported Saudi Arabia in the Yemeni conflict, although its role has been limited. Publicado también por: The New York Times - World, Al Jazeera English. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: How a hospital ship helps buoy China’s strategic mission in Africa
item.description: By the time the Chinese navy hospital ship had docked in the Guinean capital Conakry earlier this month, patients were already queuing for free consultations. The queues in front of the Auspicious Ark were so long that some people were told to come back the next day, according to Guinean media reports. The ship, operated by the PLA Navy, offers a range of medical services wherever it stops, including surgery to treat cataracts, appendicitis and hernias as well as gynaecological care. On this... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Lion droppings yield previously unknown microbial species, exposing hidden diversity inside Africa's big cats
item.description: Scientists know a great deal about how lions hunt, breed and survive, but the microscopic communities living inside them have remained largely unexplored. Now, a study of wild lions in Namibia is beginning to change that, while revealing how much biology is still missing from the world's genomic databases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Plover, not a fighter: masked lapwing nesting on Tasmanian cricket ground indifferent as play continues
item.description: While masked lapwings have a reputation for swooping during nesting season, Windsor Park oval’s resident plover just wants a good innings At Windsor Park in Riverside, just outside Launceston in northern Tasmania, a masked lapwing has claimed prime real estate in the middle of a community sports ground, showing complete indifference to the weekend cricket matches taking place around it. Warming a nest of eggs, the bird has been affectionately dubbed “Faf Swoop Plessis” by locals – a play on former South African cricket captain Faf du Plessis. Continue reading...
